rounds.text: MPS Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a P/E of just 21.8x [E1] despite elite capital efficiency metrics that dwarf sector benchmarks, including an ROE of 29.05% [E9] and an exceptional ROCE of 34.87% [E10]. The business pairs this profitability with robust organic momentum, highlighted by a quarterly operating margin expanding by 7 percentage points year-on-year to 34% [E31] and recent revenue growing 20.4 percent alongside a 53.0 percent surge in EBITDA [E78]. Furthermore, growth catalysts are firing across divisions: the newly launched Pre-Submission Peer Review in AJE is running well ahead of plan [E73], the Unbound Medicine acquisition has successfully expanded the billed client count to 841 from 404 [E81], and management has reiterated its forward guidance to comfortably cross INR 300 crores in EBITDA in FY27 [E72]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits at an elevated 6.66x against a book value of ₹ 349 [E2], and borrowings have increased to Rs 61 Cr following recent M&A activity [E39]. Even so, the company generated Rs 188 Cr in free cash flow with full cash conversion of 1.14x [E34, E36], leaving the stock backed by powerful fundamentals and concrete forward targets of approximately INR 1,500 crores in revenue by FY28 [E71].

Despite headline growth figures, MPS Ltd carries valuation multiples and financial risks that the evidence does not comfortably support. The stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 6.66x [E2] or up to 7.03x against sector benchmarks of 1.2x [E7], alongside a P/E of 22.24x which sits above the sector benchmark of 15.87x [E6]. Shareholder returns are entirely detached from cash distributions through dividends, as the dividend yield stands at a stark 0.00% [E4]. Furthermore, the company's historical volatility is elevated at 47.1% [E54], and its historical record includes a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.1% [E53]. Institutional interest has also cooled, with foreign institutional holding dropping from 3.71% in Dec 2023 to 1.49% as of Sep 2026 [E42]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing profitability metrics including a 29.05% ROE and 34.87% ROCE outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10], and boasts positive cash conversion and institutional money flow signals [E34, E44].

Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E4], foreign institutional holdings declined to 1.49% [E42], and historical volatility reaches 47.1% with a past drawdown of -93.1% [E53, E54]. However, citing the elevated P/B multiples of 6.66x or 7.03x [E2, E7] and a P/E of 22.24x [E6] ignores the extraordinary operational returns that justify premium pricing: ROCE sits at an elite 34.87% to 38.7% and ROE reaches up to 29.7%, absolutely eclipsing sector benchmarks of 5.89% and 4.42% respectively [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. Furthermore, the bear's emphasis on valuation discounts the DCF intrinsic value of Rs 4471 per share, which provides a massive 48.0% margin of safety over the market price of Rs 2325 [E45, E46].

Conceded: ROCE and ROE significantly outpace sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. However, the bull's reliance on a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 4471 offering a 48.0% margin of safety [E45, E46] ignores that the stock trades at a demanding price-to-book ratio of 6.66x to 7.03x against a sector benchmark of just 1.2x [E2, E7]. Furthermore, dismissing the P/E ratio of 22.24x [E6] overlooks that it trades at a substantial premium to the sector benchmark of 15.87x [E6]. Conceded: historical volatility and drawdowns belong to the past [E53, E54], but current valuation risks are compounded by a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], meaning shareholders receive zero cash return while paying a steep multiple. Finally, foreign institutional holdings have actively dropped from 3.71% in Dec 2023 to 1.49% in Sep 2026 [E42], signaling institutional exit from this premium pricing.
